text:
Maya: quick sync — we need to finalize the per-route SLO dashboard metrics and ownership. Focus: P50/P95/P99, TTFT, tokens/sec. Proposed primary keys: model, route, deployment_tag, region. Who emits what (runtime vs router vs infra)? Who owns Console panels? cc @Devin @Alan @Suzy :wave:

Devin: TTFT = request arrival -> first token out, right? also confirm unit ms vs seconds.

Alan: yes TTFT in ms. runtime should emit ttft histogram (low overhead), router can emit request counts/qps. tokens/sec is tricky — router sees tokens over time but worker-level counters are more accurate.

Suzy: Console wants per-route drilldown with default 1h window + compare to 24h baseline. Panels: latency shape heatmap, P50/P95/P99 lines, TTFT scatter/percentiles, tokens/sec (avg per minute), and error-rate sparkline. UX note: make drilldown retain route + model filter to avoid re-choosing.

Maya: proposed emission split: runtime -> redwood.runtime.ttft_ms (histogram), redwood.runtime.gen_tokens (counter). Router -> redwood.router.requests, redwood.router.latency_ms (for network/ingress). Ingestion should tag with model, route, variant, region, deployment_tag. Sampling: 1% event-sample for verbose traces, 100% for aggregates. Thoughts?

Devin: cardinality concern: variant + route + model may blow up. Recommend drop model_hash and any high-cardinality request tags. Keep only: model_name, route_name, variant (opt), region. Also we need a rollup key for "model_family" for panel groups.

Alan: agree on cardinality. Also pay attention to histogram bucket boundaries for ttft: suggest buckets: [0-5ms,5-20,20-50,50-100,100-250,250-500,500-1000,1000-5000]. That gives useful P99 for tail.

Maya: actionable metric list (copyable):
```
redwood.runtime.ttft_ms_histogram | tags: model, route, variant?, region, deployment_tag
redwood.runtime.generated_tokens_total | tags: model, route, variant?, region
redwood.runtime.token_rate_per_min | derived from generated_tokens_total by ingestion
redwood.router.requests_total | tags: route, region, routed_model
redwood.router.latency_ms | tags: route, region
redwood.runtime.kv_cache_hit_rate | tags: model, route
```

Suzy: for Console panels we'll need: aggregation windows (1m/1h/6h), downsample policy (p95/p99 exact not approx), and backfill strategy when model/version tags change. Also want an API to pin panels to a route so product teams can embed.

Devin: ingestion note: prefer emission as simple counters + histograms; do heavy transformations in the metrics pipeline to avoid runtime CPU cost. Token_rate_per_min can be pipeline-derived.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: emitter v2 rolled out to runtime-canary (flags: ttft_histograms = on, token_counter = on) :rocket:

Alan: sample metric line examples for instrumentation (prom style):
```
# histogram (runtime)
redwood_runtime_ttft_ms_bucket{model="v1-llama",route="chat",region="us-west-2",le="100"} 42
redwood_runtime_ttft_ms_sum{model="v1-llama",route="chat",region="us-west-2"} 12345
redwood_runtime_ttft_ms_count{model="v1-llama",route="chat",region="us-west-2"} 678

# counter (tokens)
redwood_runtime_generated_tokens_total{model="v1-llama",route="chat",region="us-west-2"} 123456
```

Maya: ownership proposal — runtime emits + owns correctness of ttft/histograms: @Alan; router emits request-level counters: @Devin; Console panels + alerting: @Suzy. I'll kick off RFC to lock naming and tags.

Suzy: SLO thresholds proposals (starting point, can vary by model class):
- Small models (low-cpu): P95 TTFT < 150ms, P99 < 400ms
- Medium models: P95 < 250ms, P99 < 800ms
- Large: P95 < 600ms, P99 < 2000ms
Also tokens/sec alert when sustained drop >40% vs baseline.

Devin: question re: rollout UX — should console show recommended fallback model when SLO breached? We have policy routing that can fall back to cheaper variant. Might be nice to surface that as a suggestion.

Maya: yes, surface routing policy suggestions: show alternative variants and estimated cost/latency tradeoff. We'll need a small API from routing to Console to suggest.

Alan: one last ops note: tag names must be stable; avoid changing model strings frequently (use pinned model_version tag).

Maya: action items:
1) Alan -> finalize histogram buckets + push emitter docs (due EOD Thu)
2) Devin -> update router counters + document ingestion tags (due Fri)
3) Suzy -> wire up draft Console panels and share link for review (due Mon)
4) Maya -> RFC for metric names/tags + adoption plan (kickoff today)

Maya: any objections? otherwise I'll create RFC and slack channel for dashboard rollout. :white_check_mark:

Devin: +1

Alan: +1

Suzy: +1 :raised_hands:
